Insulation test :\r\n- Check the insulation of the stator winding before and after the overhaul procedure.\r\nMultimeter is used for this purpose, with its one probe connected\r\nto the winding and other to the earth with switch selected in the resistance knob.\r\n2. Dismantling:\r\nNote: Before dismantling mark both motor housing and connection wires .\r\nThis will ensure that the boxing back procedure is smooth and there is no mismatch of parts.\r\nAlso check the direction of the motor rotation before stopping the motor for overhauling.\r\n- Dismantling can be done in two ways:\r\na. Out place :\r\n- Take out the motor from the place and keep it in a horizontal position\r\n- Open the motor from any one side\r\n- If it’s a small motor take out the rotor\r\n- If it’s a huge motor keep the rotor inside and open the bearings using a good bearing puller\r\nAfter any one of the above two processes are completed, perform the following procedure :\r\n1. Removal of Bearing Housing Cover:\r\n- While removing the bearing housing cover,\r\nnote that some motors will be having inner bearing cover tightened with nut bolts. Box up to be done as per the markings\r\n-Try out and check the Amperage. Compare with rated amperage and before overhaul amperage.\r\n(D) System Back in Service\r\n========================\r\nCarry out function test, commissioning /Test/Trial of the equipment as required and ensure to put back in Service.\r\nSource Interval Code: M060",

Insulation test :\r\n- Check the insulation of the stator winding before and after the overhaul procedure.\r\nMultimeter is used for this purpose, with its one probe connected\r\nto the winding and other to the earth with switch selected in the resistance knob.\r\n2. Dismantling:\r\nNote: Before dismantling mark both motor housing and connection wires .\r\nThis will ensure that the boxing back procedure is smooth and there is no mismatch of parts.\r\nAlso check the direction of the motor rotation before stopping the motor for overhauling.\r\n- Dismantling can be done in two ways:\r\na. In place (On board ship, it is mostly applicable for very big vertically coupled motor to load)\r\n-Removing the motor from the place by chain block\r\n- Remove the coupling and key\r\n- Keep the motor in place and fix the nuts\r\n- Open the motor from top (cooling fan side)\r\n- Take out the rotor by chain block, take out the stator winding separately\r\nb. Out place :\r\n- Take out the motor from the place and keep it in a horizontal position\r\n- Open the motor from any one side\r\n- If it’s a small motor take out the rotor\r\n- If it’s a huge motor keep the rotor inside and open the bearings using a good bearing puller\r\nAfter any one of the above two processes are completed, perform the following procedure :\r\n1. Removal of Bearing Housing Cover:\r\n- While removing the bearing housing cover,\r\nnote that some motors will be having inner bearing cover tightened with nut bolts. Remove it carefully.\r\nIn other constructions the bearing housing cover is locked with bearing by a circle clip.\r\nWhenever removing the housing cover on both sides (Driving End & Non Driving End) make sure proper\r\ncare is taken while handling.\r\n2. Removal of Bearing or Coupling :\r\n- Use a suitable puller (depends on the size of the bearing or coupling); mostly use the 3 arm puller,\r\n3. Insertion of bearings :\r\n- Clean the shaft on both ends and heat the new bearing up to 70° C to avoid tight insertion of the bearing in the shaft.\r\n4. Box back the motor:\r\n- Before boxing up the motor, do the insulation test again to compare with previous values.\r\nIf the values are on higher side, start boxing back, otherwise heat up the winding\r\nfor some more time with Halogen light.\r\n5. Box up to be done as per the markings\r\n-Try out and check the Amperage. Compare with rated amperage and before overhaul amperage.\r\n(D) System Back in Service\r\n========================\r\nCarry out function test, commissioning /Test/Trial of the equipment as required and ensure to put back in Service.\r\nSource Interval Code: M060",

Removal of Bearing Housing Cover:\r\n- While removing the bearing housing cover,\r\nnote that some motors will be having inner bearing cover tightened with nut bolts. Out place :\r\n- Take out the motor from the place and keep it in a horizontal position\r\n- Open the motor from any one side\r\n- If it’s a small motor take out the rotor\r\n- If it’s a huge motor keep the rotor inside and open the bearings using a good bearing puller\r\nAfter any one of the above two processes are completed, perform the following procedure :\r\n1. Removal of Bearing Housing Cover:\r\n- While removing the bearing housing cover,\r\nnote that some motors will be having inner bearing cover tightened with nut bolts. Box up to be done as per the markings\r\n-Try out and check the Amperage. Compare with rated amperage and before overhaul amperage.\r\n(D) System Back in Service\r\n========================\r\nCarry out function test, commissioning /Test/Trial of the equipment as required and ensure to put back in Service.\r\nSource Interval Code: M060",

Insulation test :\r\n- Check the insulation of the stator winding before and after the overhaul procedure.\r\nMultimeter is used for this purpose, with its one probe connected\r\nto the winding and other to the earth with switch selected in the resistance knob.\r\n2. Out place :\r\n- Take out the motor from the place and keep it in a horizontal position\r\n- Open the motor from any one side\r\n- If it’s a small motor take out the rotor\r\n- If it’s a huge motor keep the rotor inside and open the bearings using a good bearing puller\r\nAfter any one of the above two processes are completed, perform the following procedure :\r\n1. Removal of Bearing Housing Cover:\r\n- While removing the bearing housing cover,\r\nnote that some motors will be having inner bearing cover tightened with nut bolts.
